-14 LUFS is not the number your master has to hit. 📉

▸ Spotify plays tracks back around -14 LUFS integrated by default
▸ A louder master is simply turned down on playback
▸ What stays is the damage: flattened transients, less punch
▸ True peak at or below -1 dBTP keeps lossy encodes from clipping

A metal master should be as loud as the genre needs, not as loud as possible.

Stem mastering for a whole EP, at a package price. 🎛️

When the audit shows the same clash on several tracks, like kick against bass or vocals fighting the guitars, fixing it from a stereo file means compromise on every song. From stems, each element gets its own decision.

The Stem EP:
▸ Up to 5 tracks, up to 6 stems each
▸ An audit per track
▸ Loudness balanced across the whole EP, transitions worked out
▸ Unlimited revisions

€549 instead of €645 for five stem singles, €96 saved. Delivery in 5–7 days. Pay up front or on invoice after delivery. Incl. 19% VAT.

In doom, the space between the hits is part of the riff. 🕯️

▸ Slow tempos expose every tail: cymbals, amp sustain, room
▸ Heavy limiting pulls those tails up and flattens the swell
▸ The low end needs control below 100 Hz, not more level
▸ Dynamics carry the weight of a slow riff

Doom is mastered differently than death metal. That is the point of genre-specific work.
